title: Signum: Rome total war inspired 2d RTS
author: -pertinax-
selftext:
Long time web dev here who has dabbled in graphics and visual demos in the past. For the past few months I've been using my spare tokens left over from my main gig to work on my tribute to one of my favourite games of all time, Rome Total War.

What you see here is pixie.js as the game engine with react used for the game UI.

Sprites are built in blender and then rasterized and downsampled to get the low res pixel style I wanted. A few months ago, when models were less capable, I was painstakingly drawing the sprites with Aseprite but the results now look way better and take approximately 100x less time.

Music was generated with Gemini, and sound effects are a combination of some stuff from freesound.org and elevenlabs (which is very good).

On mobile the game can be installed as a PWA and feels somewhat native.

I'd say the main challenge is to tune the AI to give the gane a feeling of balance and overall to make it feel fun and draw you back for another go. I'm pretty happy with where it is right now but more work is still needed on the career mode balance and tuning. Just lots and lots of playtesting is needed for that.

If you are interested to try it is online at playsignum.xyz

comments.author: COLES-BRAND-NUTMEG
comments.body:
Looks real good. I’m always happy to see more TW-style games.

I have a suggestion to make. All tactics / strategy games fall short in one aspect: enemy AI.

When you have learned its patterns each battle becomes routine. The only threat left is an ever increasing number of enemies and cheaty-stats boosts.

The thrill of outsmarting the enemy never occurs again.

The reason for this is that developers - with good reason - only make their AI good enough. There’s too much attention to pour elsewhere. How good does AI need to be anyway?

I say it should be great.

The best way to achieve greatness is to aim to make an AI that cannot be beat. One that will always outsmart you, react faster than you, and in all ways surpass you in any and all decisions it makes.

When it is so good that you stand absolutely no chance to defeat it - you then introduce believable errors.

Communication delays. Unreliable information. Weighted decisions informed by miscalculation, haste or indecisiveness. Great AI doesn’t mean it cannot be beat. It means it believably acts under constraints that suit the model it aims to represent.

An example of bad AI:

Chess.com bots do not fall for tricks or forget about your sniper bishop. They just randomly make a blunder, inaccuracy, miss, good, best or great move. The higher their rating, the more they’re likely to make better moves. The best strategy to win against high ranked bots is to play cautiously until it makes a randomised blunder. It has none of the depth or variety a game against a player possesses.

An example of what great AI could be:

There‘a a scene in Saving Private Ryan where an American and German soldier come face to face. They both empty their guns without killing one another. The German, in confusion, throws his helmet at him. The American, shaken and wounded thinks of nothing better to do than to throw his. He forgot he had a sidearm.

It’s an absurd situation. But it’s entirely believable. Can you imagine a FPS that had soldiers lose composure when stressed? Increasing the chance of them making mistakes - to the point of the absurdity above? What if composure was bound by experience such that an untrained soldier would quickly break under pressure while elites would withstand much more? And what if their reactions couldn’t be predicted?

There is a wealth of untapped depth across all game genres in the form of great AI and never more so than in RTS.

Game AI has not improved in 20 years. There has never been a better time than now.

Good luck with the game!

replies.author: -pertinax-
replies.body: Thank you for these great suggestions. I agree with everything you say. It strikes me that with AI assisted development there really is scope to push this aspect very far indeed. You've given me a lot to chew on, cheers!

replies.author: COLES-BRAND-NUTMEG
replies.body: It’s my pleasure! Yes I agree. I think we are on the verge of great things.
